title: Griffin Gaming Partners acquired a stake in tinyBuild
summary: TinyBuild, the publisher of Hello Neighbor, Potion Craft, The King is Watching, and many other games, has gained a new shareholder. That shareholder is the venture capital firm Griffin Gaming Partners.

title: Rumor: Microsoft has temporarily stopped adding new games from third-party studios to Game Pass
summary: It’s possible that Microsoft hasn’t been signing contracts with third-party developers who wish to add games to the Game Pass subscription for some time. At least, that’s what claims Fernando Rizo, former sales director at Raw Fury and now a partner at Caboodle Games.

title: 007 First Light was the highest-grossing game in May in the US
summary: Circana analyst Mat Piscatella continues to share data on the U.S. gaming market. He published detailed statistics for May, which include information on revenue and top blockbusters.

title: WN Istanbul’26 took place in Turkey. We share the results
summary: Last week, WN Istanbul’26 took place in Istanbul — the tenth anniversary Turkish event for game developers and publishers organized by WN Media Group. Here’s what happened at the event.

title: Google Play is preparing to reduce its commission in the European Union, the United Kingdom, and the United States
summary: Google Corporation has confirmed that it still plans to reduce the commission rate in its app store. It first announced its intentions back in March ahead of the conclusion of its long-standing legal battles with Epic Games.

title: Stronghold 4 has garnered over 250,000 wishlists
summary: Steam users have shown great interest in the new installment of the legendary strategy franchise Stronghold. They added Stronghold 4 to their wishlists a quarter of a million times within just two weeks of the game’s announcement.

title: Report: Tencent May Sell Its Stake in Several Japanese Studios
summary: The Chinese giant Tencent is preparing to divest some of its gaming assets in Japan, reports Bloomberg, citing sources.

title: Obsidian Entertainment accused of skimping on salaries
summary: Obsidian Entertainment has faced a lawsuit in the United States. The company was sued by former employees who claim it violated California labor laws.

title: Sony has officially removed the release of single-player games on PC from its business strategy
summary: Every June, Sony submits a comprehensive annual report to the U.S. Securities and Exchange Commission (SEC), detailing its business strategy among other things. As noted by Game File journalist Stephen Totilo, this time the company introduced several significant changes regarding its gaming division’s operations.

title: The crisis didn’t prevent the gaming market from setting a revenue record in 2025, according to analytics
summary: The analytics company Newzoo has finally summed up the results for the global video game market in 2025—before this, they had released several forecasts. As it turns out, last year became the most profitable in monetary terms in the history of observations, despite numerous layoffs and studio closures.

title: The European Commission did not support the initiative to preserve the Stop Killing Games
summary: The authors of the Stop Killing Games initiative, aimed at preventing the deactivation of games purchased by gamers, were unable to secure support from the European Commission. The agency officially stated that “at this stage,” it cannot intervene and amend EU legislation.

title: Report: Xbox intends to close several studios at once
summary: Microsoft’s gaming division may undergo significant “downsizing.” As reported by Bloomberg journalist Jason Schreier, XBOX is preparing to part ways with at least three teams.

title: Valve has once again been accused of having a monopoly in the PC market — this time in the Netherlands
summary: A Dutch NGO, The Consumer Competition Claims Foundation (CCCF), has taken a stand against the owner of Steam.

title: Case Study: How The One Game Studio Hit 170% D1 ROAS and Achieved a 1.26x Ad LTV Lift with ByteBrew Ads
summary: Kian Hozouri, COO and co-founder of ByteBrew, shared in his Game World Observer column how his startup helped The One Game Studio achieve impressive results in ROAS and Ad LTV growth.

title: Ubisoft to lay off several hundred employees and close two studios
summary: Restructuring is ongoing at Ubisoft. This has been reported by the media, referencing an internal company letter.

title: ESA is concerned that the American bill against deepfakes could harm video games
summary: This week, a bill aimed at combating deepfakes will be reviewed in the United States. Although the initiative does not directly concern video games, it could still have an impact on them—and not in a positive way. At least, that’s the perspective of the Entertainment Software Association (ESA).

title: Nintendo was fined 35 million euros due to Joy-Con stick drift
summary: In France, an investigation into Nintendo related to defective Joy-Con controller sticks has concluded. The outcome was not in the company’s favor.

title: Report: Supercell conducted layoffs in its North American division
summary: The workforce of Supercell has become smaller, reports MobileGamer, referencing posts from laid-off employees on social media.

title: The WN Istanbul’26 program has been announced. Among the participants are Rovio, Epic Games Store, Rollic Games, PlaySide Studios, and many others
summary: In two weeks, on June 18 and 19, a business event for game developers and publishers, WN Istanbul’26, will take place in Turkey. Here’s what’s on the event’s agenda.

title: The WN Growth Summit took place in Limassol. Here are the highlights
summary: Last week on May 28, one of Cyprus’s largest cities hosted the WN Growth Summit Limassol’26. It focused on the growth challenges of the gaming business. Below are the key outcomes of the event.

title: Gabe Newell on the accusations of Steam’s monopoly: “Customers have enormous choice where they purchase their products”
summary: In 2023, Valve’s head Gabe Newell provided testimony in a legal case against Wolfire Games, which accused the company of monopolizing the PC store market. A transcript of his speech was recently obtained by Bloomberg.

title: Atari just got bigger: it has acquired the creators of Crossy Road
summary: Atari continues its spree of M&A deals. This time, it announced the acquisition of the studio Hipster Whale.
